synonyms: Opuntia engelmannii subsp. lindheimeri (Engelm.) U.Guzmán & Mandujano
taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and ITIS as Opuntia engelmannii var. lindheimeri. The project's source row Opuntia lindheimeri is a synonym and is deliberately merged into this single learner concept.
look_here_first: Find an areole before anything else. On the flattened green cladodes, each areole is a specialized short shoot that can carry hairs, glochids, permanent spines, flowers, or new pads. Then compare pad shape, spine/glochid pattern, yellow-to-orange flower, and beet-red berry.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve north Hays County natural-flora list includes O. engelmannii var. lindheimeri as naturally occurring. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Cactaceae herbarium index includes three specimens. Williamson — UT PRC Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment. Kerr — Texas Parks and Wildlife Kerr WMA flora documents O. engelmannii var. lindheimeri in native vegetation.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Exact county documentation only; the synonym O. lindheimeri is not counted as a separate species.

best_field_traits: succulent shrub made of flattened photosynthetic cladodes/pads
true defining cactus structure is the areole
areoles arranged across pads and bearing glochids plus zero to several permanent spines
glochids tiny, barbed, irritating, and clustered at areoles
pads commonly obovate and green to bluish-green/glaucous
large radial flowers usually yellow to yellow-orange
inferior ovary surrounded by stem/pericarpel tissue bearing areoles
many-seeded fleshy berry, beet-red with purple-red pulp
morphology_keys.areole: A specialized axillary short shoot. Learn this before 'spines': flowers, new stems, hairs, glochids and permanent spines arise from areoles.
morphology_keys.stem: The familiar pad is a flattened photosynthetic stem segment (cladode), not an ordinary leaf.
morphology_keys.spines: Permanent spines vary greatly even within the variety; do not require a fixed spine count. Glochids are smaller barbed deciduous spines clustered in the areole.
morphology_keys.flower: Large radial flower with numerous graded perianth segments and more than 200 free stamens in the detailed Williamson County treatment.
morphology_keys.ovary: Inferior; outer stem tissue around it bears tubercles/areoles.
morphology_keys.fruit: Many-seeded fleshy berry, commonly broadly obovoid/top-shaped and beet-colored, with mucilaginous purple-red pulp.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Confirm Cactaceae first from true areoles. Within Opuntia, use pad shape, areole spacing, glochid color, permanent-spine number/position, flower and mature fruit together rather than one spine character.
